jobs.description:
Principal Consultant / Technical Director – Ecotoxicology & Ecological Risk Assessment

Lead Technical Excellence. Shape Strategy. Grow a Market-Leading Practice.

Are you an established Ecotoxicologist or Ecological Risk Assessor
looking for an opportunity to build your profile, influence major projects, and help shape the future direction of a growing environmental consultancy practice?

We are seeking an experienced Principal Consultant or Technical Director
to join and lead our Ecotoxicology and Ecological Risk Assessment group as part of the Toxicology & Risk team
. This is a key technical and business role for a recognised industry professional with a strong technical reputation, established client relationships, and a passion for growing business and developing people.

As a key member within our Soils, Geochemistry, Toxicology and Risk Practice
, you will work alongside a highly regarded team of specialist consultants, including a dedicated ecotoxicology group and a broader multidisciplinary practice of more than 40+ experts across Asia Pacific.

This is more than a technical leadership role. It is an opportunity to join a collaborative team that combines deep technical expertise with a strong growth mindset. You will have the autonomy to shape the direction of the ecotoxicology practice while being supported by a substantial multidisciplinary network of specialists who are solving some of the most complex environmental challenges across the region.

We have just over 1,200 staff in Asia Pacific and you will find us located in all the major cities and many regional areas. We are open to location for the successful person where we have established offices in place.

Responsibilities

Working with other technical specialists who are passionate about their fields and highly collaborative employees, this role offers the platform to:

Lead and grow a successful ecotoxicology and ecological risk assessment capability.
Drive business development and work-winning initiatives across existing and emerging markets.
Leverage your professional network and industry profile to identify opportunities and develop long-term client partnerships.
Provide technical leadership on complex environmental, contaminated land, mining, industrial, infrastructure and regulatory projects.
Mentor and develop a team of talented ecotoxicologists and risk assessment specialists.
Collaborate with leading experts across contaminated land, geochemistry, toxicology, human health risk assessment, hydrogeology and environmental sciences.
Influence strategic direction, service offerings and market growth within a well-established environmental consulting business.

Experience

Not only will you be a honest, trusted and great person to be around, you will also be a recognised technical leader who brings:

Relevant tertiary qualifications in ecotoxicology, environmental science, ecology, toxicology or a related discipline coupled with 10-15+ years’ experience (ideally within a consulting environment but open to other industry)
A strong reputation within industry, regulatory, government and/or commercial sectors.
Demonstrated success in winning work, developing client relationships and generating revenue growth.
Established networks and connections that can contribute to the continued expansion of the practice.
Experience leading multidisciplinary project teams and mentoring technical professionals.
Strong commercial acumen and the ability to identify and capitalise on market opportunities.
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

Our Benefits

We are most proud of our expert teams and unique culture where we work together to collaborate on projects to get the best possible outcome for our clients.

Whether you’re enjoying our flexible hybrid work environment, taking advantage of our novated leasing offers, or at a time in your life where a supportive and generous parental leave scheme is key, our benefits aim to ensure that we cater for all.

You can find a comprehensive list here.

Next Steps

If leading an established and premier team at a global multidisciplinary consultancy is your next career move, apply now with a copy of your CV and cover letter.

Unsolicited resumes from recruitment consultants will not be accepted. You must be part of the preferred supplier agreement list which is coordinated through our Talent Acquisition team.

jobs.title: Watershed Scientist
jobs.description:
**About the Organization**

Heal the Bay is the most recognized environmental nonprofit group in LA for a reason: we have been keeping Southern California's coastal waters and watersheds safe, healthy, and clean for people and marine life since 1985. Using education, science, advocacy, and community action, we raise awareness and make progress with practical solutions to often complex problems. We conduct hundreds of beach and community cleanups each year, informing people about the root causes of pollution along the shorelines and in their neighborhoods. We advocate for strict water quality regulations that protect the health of both humans and the animals that call local creeks, rivers, and the Santa Monica Bay home. We operate the award-winning Heal the Bay Aquarium at the Santa Monica Pier, inspiring visitors to become stewards for the region’s most important natural resource: clean water. We also educate and inspire the next generation of environmental stewards, with more than 10,000 students joining us each year for school field trips, science-based classroom presentations, and events. Learn more about us at www.healthebay.org/our-impact

**About the Role**

The Watershed Scientist leads the day-to-day management of Heal the Bay’s Stream Team and River Report Card programs, which combine freshwater quality monitoring, workforce development, and public health communication. The Stream Team trains local students in field and laboratory techniques while monitoring freshwater recreational sites in the Malibu Creek and Los Angeles River watersheds. The River Report Card provides weekly water quality grades and annual reporting for freshwater recreation sites across Los Angeles County, including but not limited to the sites monitored by the Stream Team, helping the public understand pollution risks and informing efforts to identify and address sources of contamination. These initiatives aim to equip the public with the information they need to protect themselves from harmful pollution in freshwater recreational waters, and to identify and address potential sources of contamination that could impact water quality.

The Watershed Scientist also supports the Beach Report Card in collaboration with the Water Quality Data Specialist and leads policy and advocacy efforts to protect and improve freshwater recreational water quality. This includes addressing bacterial pollution, sewage spill protocols and notifications, and riparian habitat; engaging with regulatory agencies and other stakeholders; and advocating for improved monitoring, pollution prevention, and restoration.

The Watershed Scientist collaborates across Heal the Bay’s departments on campaigns, education, and outreach. This position reports to the Associate Director of Science & Policy.

**Expectations & Responsibilities**

* Manage the Stream Team;
  + Hire, train, and mentor water quality monitors during the summer season.
  + Coordinate sampling schedules and field activities, ensuring data quality and compliance with established methods.
  + Oversee data collection and analysis for bacteria monitoring and water quality grading at freshwater recreation sites
  + Manage databases and calculate weekly River Report Card grades.
  + Conduct occasional field and laboratory work to assess bacteria levels in freshwater areas.
  + Support outreach and education efforts by updating content, sharing stories of the Stream Team’s work, and promoting public engagement with freshwater quality monitoring data.
  + Update the Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) and implement QA/QC procedures.
  + Develop a freshwater HAB monitoring program in coordination with the State Water Resources Control Board.
  + Explore opportunities to improve and expand the Stream Team Program.
* Manage the River Report Card Program;
  + Publish weekly River Report Card grades and updates on Heal the Bay’s River Report Card website.
  + Ensure accurate display of grades, historical data, and site information, collaborating with the communications and technology teams to maintain data accuracy and accessibility.
  + Lead the writing of the River Report Card report focused on the most recent annual grades.
  + Lead development of a River Report Card manuscript for long-term data analysis.
  + Explore opportunities to improve the website’s functionality, user experience, and data presentation.
* Lead policy and advocacy work for recreational water quality
  + Track, analyze, comment on, and advocate for water quality protection and improvements related to recreational waterbodies, focused on bacterial pollution, sewage spill protocols and notifications, and riparian habitat;
  + Represent Heal the Bay’s positions at public meetings, hearings and other forums; participate in water quality workgroups, TACs, watershed and river coalitions, including LA River;
  + Maintain, cultivate and establish relationships with recreational water quality monitoring agencies for freshwater sites in Los Angeles County;
  + Create and maintain relationships with government staff, advocacy groups, scientific researchers and other environmental stakeholders;
  + Engage in AB 1066 (Bloom, 2021) implementation by making recommendations to the California Water Quality Monitoring Council for a definition of a priority freshwater recreation area and elements of a statewide monitoring program; work towards new legislation to require that inland recreational waters are regularly monitored;
* Participate in inter-departmental projects and Heal the Bay campaigns:
  + Collaborate with other staff on education, outreach, and policy initiatives.
  + Participate in Science & Policy department meetings.
  + Coordinate with the communications team for public outreach, updates, and media requests related to the River Report Card and Stream Team programs.

**Experience & Skills**

* Passion for Heal the Bay’s mission and protecting environmental and public health in Southern California’s freshwater and

jobs.title: Environmental Protection Specialist
jobs.description:
**Summary**
-----------

This position is located in the Occupational Safety & Health Service of the VA Medical Center in Martinez, CA.

Learn more about this agency

  

**This job is open to**
-----------------------

### **The public**

U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.

  

**Duties**
----------

\*\***\*THIS IS NOT A VIRTUAL POSITION, YOU MUST LIVE WITHIN OR BE WILLING TO RELOCATE WITHIN A COMMUTABLE DISTANCE OF THE DUTY LOCATION\*\*\***
  
  
The primary purpose of this position is to ensure that the VA Health Care System maintains full compliance with all applicable Federal, State, and local environmental laws and regulations; Executive Orders; and VA/VHA directives. The Environmental Protection Specialist provides leadership, oversight, and coordination of the facility's Green Environmental Management System (GEMS) to improve environmental performance, reduce risk, and support continual improvement in alignment with ISO 14001 principles. The Environmental Protection Specialist establishes environmental objectives and targets, based upon the significant environmental aspects, on an annual basis in order to pursue continual improvement of environmental performance.
  
  
The Environmental Protection Specialist plays a critical role in planning, developing, and administering environmental programs addressing the impacts of VA operations on air, land, water, and other environmental media. This includes establishing effective operational controls, monitoring compliance, facilitating corrective actions, and advising leadership on environmental requirements that influence healthcare operations and patient safety.
  
  
In carrying out these responsibilities, the employee embraces and supports the guiding principles of Health Service Area (HAS) 5.2, performing all duties in a manner that promotes patient safety, high-quality healthcare, regulatory stewardship, and outstanding customer service. The incumbent fosters a collaborative, team-based approach to environmental management and contributes to an organizational culture dedicated to serving Veterans by maintaining safe, compliant, and sustainable facilities
  
  
**Work Schedule:** Monday through Friday, 8:00am - 4:30pm.
  
**Recruitment & Relocation Incentives:** Not authorized.
  
**Telework:** This position may be authorized for telework. Telework eligibility will be discussed during the interview process.

  

**Requirements**
----------------

### **Conditions of employment**

* You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this job
* **To be considered for this position, you must complete all required steps in the process.** In addition to the application and questionnaire, this position requires an online assessment. The online assessment measures critical general competencies required to perform the job.
* All applicants tentatively selected for VA employment in a testing designated position are subject to urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Applicants who refuse to be tested will be denied employment with VA.
* Selective Service Registration is required for males born after 12/31/1959
* Physical Requirements: The work required does not inherently include any physical requirements essential for successful job performance that could not otherwise be performed with accommodation or workplace adjustment. A pre-placement physical examination is not required.
* Subject to background/security investigation
* Selected applicants will be required to complete an online onboarding process. Acceptable form(s) of identification will be required to complete pre-employment requirements (https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-acceptable-documents). Effective May 7, 2025, driver's licenses or state-issued identification cards that are not REAL ID compliant cannot be utilized as an acceptable form of identification for employment.
* Participation in the seasonal influenza vaccination program is a requirement for all Department of Veterans Affairs Health Care Personnel (HCP) - See "Required Documents" below for details.

As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1-year probationary period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider:

* your performance and conduct;
* the needs and interests of the agency;
* whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and
* whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service.

Upon completion of your probationary, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.

### **Qualifications**

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: One year specialized experience that equipped you with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position, and that is typically in or related to the work of the position to be filled. To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the GS-09 grade level in Federal service. Examples of qualifying experience include: ensuring environmental performance and compliance of a health care system/facility; leading review processes to assess risks, waste streams, and waste management practices; and overseeing operational controls that protect human health and the environment from chemical, biological, and physical hazards. This experience must be detailed in your resume to receive credit. ~OR~
  
  
A Ph.D., equivalent doctoral degree, 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree, or an LL.M. in a related field that demonstrates your ability to perform the duties of this position. Transcripts required. ~OR~
  
  
An equivalent combination of specialized experience and progressivel

jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking an experienced and driven Client Account Manager - Air Quality focused
with expertise in air quality compliance (permitting, stack testing, ambient air monitoring) and account management to support business growth and client engagement. This role is ideal for a proven sales leader with an existing book of clients, strong relationship management skills, and a deep understanding of air quality strategies. The selected candidate will be responsible for identifying and securing new business opportunities, driving revenue growth, and delivering innovative environmental solutions.

This hybrid position can be based out of AECOM's offices in Houston, TX; Austin, TX; Chicago, IL; Cincinnati, OH; Denver, CO; Fort Collins, CO; Minneapolis, MN; or Orange, CA. We are also open to candidates not located in these geographic areas.

Key Responsibilities include:

Develop and execute business strategies to expand AECOM’s air quality compliance services.
Maintain and grow existing client relationships while identifying new opportunities in the public and private sectors.
Leverage an existing book of clients to generate sales and secure high-value environmental projects.
Work closely with internal teams to develop and present proposals, technical solutions, and service offerings.
Negotiate contracts and service agreements to align with client needs and financial objectives.
Provide industry insight and stay updated on air quality regulations, compliance standards, and emerging trends.
Support cross-business collaboration to provide integrated environmental solutions across multiple sectors.
Meet or exceed sales targets while contributing to the long-term strategic vision of AECOM.

About AECOM’s Environment Business Line

Join AECOM to be part of an expert global team who is connected through a well-developed, worldwide, internal technical practice network through which you can learn from and brainstorm with the best in the world. AECOM is an industry-leading, world class environmental firm, and we want you to succeed within it. We respect and encourage your own pathway to excellence via our Freedom to Grow initiative.

AECOM is known for our award-winning technical excellence, leading-edge science and innovative project delivery. We provide sustainable solutions for some of the world’s most challenging issues. Our global clients and their projects span a variety of market sectors and geographies and require innovative technical solutions to solve wide-ranging environmental problems.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, engineering, business, or related field.
8 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education in managing client accounts, sales and drive business development within air quality compliance services.
Travel of 25-50% will be required, as this is a client facing role.
A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree is preferred.
10+ years of experience in account management, sales, and air quality compliance services.
Proven ability to manage client accounts and drive business development initiatives.
Strong understanding of air quality regulations, permitting, and compliance.
Experience leading large-scale environmental compliance projects.
Established industry relationships with clients in government, energy, commercial, and industrial sectors.
Experience in contract negotiations, sales forecasting, and revenue management.
Ability to work in a matrixed organization, coordinating across multiple teams and disciplines.
Proficiency in CRM tools, data analytics, and sales tracking platforms.

Additional Information

Relocation is not available for this position.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $165000 to $215000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Job Description And Duties

The Regulatory and Risk Modeling (RRM) Section within the Modeling and Meteorology Branch (MMB) is responsible for conducting the triennial California Air Toxics Assessment (CATA) and maintaining the CATA visualization mapping tool and data portal, as well as providing microscale to statewide air quality and toxics modeling support for the Air Board's various regulatory programs, including the community air protection program, airborne toxic control measures, state implementation plans for lead, NO2, and SO2, the air toxics hot spots program, and emergency response support.

The APS, working as part of a team, will support CATA through preparing and QA/QC'ing model inputs, such as emissions inventory, meteorology, and boundary conditions, conduct air dispersion and chemical transport modeling, investigate emerging air toxics (e.g., PCBTF, EtO, acrolein), translate ambient exposure to estimated cancer risk, analyze model outputs, and summarize findings for both technical and public audiences. In addition, the APS will work closely with lead staff on supporting the day-to-day operation of the High Performance Computing (HPC) Linux modeling cluster CATA modeling relies on. This could include monitoring storage and compute node usage, troubleshooting any issues that may arise, and onboarding new users.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of hybrid telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location at their own expense, as indicated on their duty statement.

jobs.title: Early-Career Hazardous Materials Consultant - Perth, WA
jobs.description:
Build on your asbestos surveying experience and grow your specialist career
Work alongside industry experts who will support your technical development
Perth based with opportunities to work on diverse projects across WA and beyond

An exciting opportunity for an early-career Hazardous Materials Consultant to develop their skills and experience within our established Workplace Health and Safety team. You'll gain exposure to a diverse range of projects, supported by experienced professionals who are committed to helping you grow.

Why Join Our Team?

Joining our team means you'll work alongside experienced scientists, engineers and specialist consultants, gaining valuable exposure to hazardous materials and occupational hygiene projects across a range of industries.

We provide specialist services to Tier 1 Mining and Oil & Gas companies, Defence, Federal and State government agencies, and other major clients. Our projects range from local site investigations to some of the largest and most recognised projects across WA and the NT, with opportunities for exposure to international work.

Working closely with the broader Tetra Tech family of companies, we combine technical expertise with practical, sustainable solutions to help our clients manage complex environmental and workplace health challenges.

You'll be joining a supportive team where you can build on your existing fieldwork experience, broaden your technical knowledge and develop your career with guidance from highly qualified professionals.

About The Role

With a strong pipeline of projects across our national Workplace Health and Safety team, we're looking for an early-career Hazardous Materials Consultant to join our growing Perth team.

This opportunity is ideally suited to someone with at least 2 years' experience in asbestos surveying and hazardous materials inspections who is looking to take the next step in their consulting career.

You'll be involved in a mix of fieldwork, technical reporting and client engagement, with opportunities to develop your skills across hazardous materials assessments and occupational hygiene services.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Undertaking asbestos and hazardous materials surveys, assessments and site inspections
Conducting field investigations, sampling and monitoring activities
Assisting with occupational hygiene monitoring and asbestos fibre counting
Supporting asbestos removal and remediation projects, including site inspections and clearance activities where appropriately qualified
Collecting, recording and interpreting field data, ensuring accuracy and quality
Preparing hazardous materials registers, survey reports and other technical documentation
Liaising with clients, contractors and colleagues to support safe and effective project delivery
Assisting senior consultants with project coordination and delivery

About You

We're looking for someone who enjoys hands-on fieldwork, has a genuine interest in hazardous materials and is keen to continue learning and developing their technical expertise.

Ideally, You'll Bring

A minimum of 2 years' practical experience in asbestos surveying, hazardous materials inspections or a closely related field
Qualifications in a relevant science discipline, occupational hygiene or a related field
A sound understanding of asbestos identification, sampling and hazardous materials assessment practices
Experience preparing asbestos registers, survey reports or other technical documentation
Good communication skills and the confidence to engage with clients and contractors on site
Strong attention to detail, a practical approach to problem-solving and a commitment to safe work practices
A willingness to learn, contribute to the team and develop your technical capabilities
The flexibility to travel to regional and remote sites as required
A current full Australian driver's licence
Australian citizenship or permanent residency to meet Defence project requirements

Experience in occupational hygiene monitoring, asbestos air monitoring or fibre counting would be advantageous, but is not essential.

Holding a Licensed Asbestos Assessor qualification, or working towards eligibility, would also be highly regarded.

Please note:
This role will involve fieldwork and travel to regional and remote locations, including occasional periods away from home.

The Perks You’ll Love

Work-Life Balance: While this role is essentially field based, you have the ability to buy extra leave giving you up to 8 weeks leave per year!
Diverse Projects: Work across a wide variety of projects, clients, and sectors
Growth Opportunities: Professional development, coaching, and mentorship from our top experts
Memberships: Professional memberships to help you stay ahead in your field
Recognition: Our reward and recognition program makes sure your hard work doesn’t go unnoticed
Ownership: Participate in our employee stock purchase plan
Parental Leave: Paid leave for both primary and secondary caregivers
Support: Employee assistance program for you and your immediate family
Travel Discounts: Great deals through our corporate traveller program
Car Leasing: Take advantage of novated vehicle leasing options

About Us

Tetra Tech Coffey provides high-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients.

With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation. 

Our commitment to creating lasting, measurable value is reflected in our global  1 Billion People Challenge , which tracks how our 100,000+ annual projects benefit people and communities around the world.

Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  
  
Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I, the incumbent performs professional scientific analyses and fieldwork associated with appropriate use of pesticides and serves as a Central Region lead on various complex pesticide use enforcement programs and issues. The incumbent provides leadership and motivation in accomplishing CRO’s program functions and objectives; is a resource for and trains both county and DPR staff; and provides education and outreach for professional organizations. The incumbent is instrumental in facilitating and maintaining a collaborative working environment.
  
  
The Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) will work closely with the Environmental Scientists assigned in Product Compliance to assure compliance with the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) and USEPA/State pesticide and environmental protection laws and regulations. Our team is a dynamic, passionate, and diverse group of scientists, engineers, toxicologists, analysts, and administrative staff working to protect California's people and the environment by advancing the design, development, and use of chemically safer products.
  
  
SCP is seeking a Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to lead efforts to implement laws banning certain chemicals in consumer products, including developing regulations and conducting compliance and enforcement activities. This position is under the general direction of a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory). Learn more by visiting our homepage at https://www.dtsc.ca.gov/SCP/.
  
  
**The Senior Environmental Scientist will have the opportunity to:**

* Conduct technical research and data analysis to support the development of regulations, compliance sampling plans, and enforcement strategies, including identifying manufacturers and evaluating covered products to understand the scope of regulated products sold in California;
* Draft rulemaking packages and prepare documentation to implement statutory and regulatory requirements in compliance with the Administrative Procedures Act;
* Organize and facilitate pre-regulatory workshops, public meetings, and external engagement activities, including outreach to manufacturers, retailers, and other interested parties;
* Assist with compliance and enforcement activities, including conducting investigations, preparing notices of violation, and developing documentation to support enforcement actions;
* Mentor team members to ensure the effective and successful implementation of newly enacted legislation and departmental goals.
* Develop compliance sampling plans and support the procurement and cataloging of samples for laboratory testing;
* Analyze testing results and review documents submitted by responsible entities to assess compliance with chemical bans;
* Provide technical assistance and compliance support to responsible entities, including manufacturers and retailers;
* Lead the preparation of public-facing resources such as guidance documents, fact sheets, and website content to keep interested parties informed of compliance requirements and enforcement actions; and
* Prepare reports to inform the Legislature, the public, department leadership, and agency management of compliance and enforcement updates.

**Job Overview**

As an Environmental Specialist, you’ll help clients address environmental requirements through fieldwork, research, analysis, and clear technical reporting. You’ll support projects from permitting through implementation, applying environmental regulatory compliance practices to protect public health and natural resources. * Use geographic information systems (GIS), including ArcGIS, to organize and analyze spatial data; apply Microsoft Office tools to prepare technical reports.
* Communicate findings and project updates to clients and team members, including work related to water treatment.

Your impact: Reliable sampling and clear analysis help clients make informed decisions that support compliance and public health.

**Requirements**

* Experience practicing in an environmental science role, such as environmental consulting, with environmental field sampling and outdoor work experience.
* Technical writing and technical report writing skills, with strong research, data collection, data analysis, and analysis skills.
* Working knowledge of environmental regulatory compliance, environmental compliance, and environmental law; familiarity with EPA requirements and OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration) practices.
* Technical proficiency with GIS and ArcGIS, Microsoft Office, and project management tools or methods.
* Laboratory experience and the ability to communicate technical information clearly to clients; water treatment experience is useful.

### **Position Description & Qualifications**

  
  

Serco is seeking an **Environmental Data Review & Validation Chemist** to support the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s Laboratory Services and Applied Science Division (LSASD) in Fort Meade, Maryland.

As a member of Serco’s Environmental Service Assistance Team, you will collaborate with EPA scientists and staff to review and validate Contract Laboratory Program (CLP) data. Your work will contribute directly to the EPA’s mission of protecting human health and the environment.

Serco offers a collaborative environment with opportunities to expand your technical knowledge, strengthen your analytical skills, and contribute to meaningful environmental initiatives.

**In This Role, You Will**
--------------------------

* Review and validate organic analytical data, including volatile organic compounds, semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, PCBs, dioxins, and PCB congeners, using applicable EPA National Functional Guidelines and regional standard operating procedures.
* Validate metals data generated through inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) in accordance with applicable National Functional Guidelines.
* Prepare detailed, accurate, and professional reports documenting data-review findings.
* Manage and maintain electronic analytical data across multiple platforms.
* Monitor workflow, backlogs, deliverables, and performance metrics.
* Review standard operating procedures as needed.
* Track and analyze key performance indicators to identify trends and support continuous improvement.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

To be successful in this role, you must have:

* A bachelor’s degree in chemistry or a related scientific field.
* At least two years of experience working in environmental laboratories or with EPA analytical methods. An advanced degree may substitute for some professional experience.
* At least one year of experience reviewing and validating analytical data.
* Extensive experience performing gas chromatography (GC) or gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analyses using one or more of the following:
  + EPA Contract Laboratory Program Statements of Work
  + EPA SW-846 methods
  + EPA drinking-water methods
  + Other applicable organic or inorganic analytical methods
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365.
* The ability to obtain an EPA Public Trust clearance.
* Strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills.
* A strong background in analyzing and interpreting complex scientific data.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

The following experience and skills are preferred:

* At least three years of experience working as an organic or inorganic chemist or laboratory technician.
* Experience with laboratory quality-control programs and analytical data review or validation.
* Experience reviewing or analyzing one or more of the following:
  + Dioxins and PCB congeners using high-resolution gas chromatography-mass spectrometry

jobs.description:
**Melbourne, Victoria, Australia | On-Site | Full Time**

We are seeking an Environmental Scientist to deliver environmental investigations and project work in Melbourne (VIC). This role suits a scientist with a few years of experience who is confident working independently in the field and ready to take on more ownership. You will lead field activities, look after our laboratory data processes, support report writing, and help train junior team members while continuing to build towards a senior role.

**What you will do**

* Undertake fieldwork including soil, landfill and ground gas, vapour, groundwater, leachate and asbestos sampling
* Conduct inspections and compliance monitoring, including supervising subcontractors on site
* Manage laboratory Chain of Custody processes, the COC register and the ESDAT data platform
* Maintain field equipment and supplies in the warehouse to prevent cross-contamination
* Collect and interpret data, and contribute to technical reports
* Assist senior staff with scopes of work, fee proposals, report writing, and project documentation
* Train and support junior staff in fieldwork activities
* Prepare safety documentation including Health and Safety Management Plans, JSAs and SWMS
* Contribute to business development activities where appropriate

**What we are looking for**

* Degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Geoscience or a related discipline
* At least 3 years of relevant industry experience
* Demonstrated ability to work independently in field and project environments
* Well-developed problem solving and analytical skills
* Sound understanding of relevant Australian Standards and environmental legislation
* Experience with ESDAT or similar environmental data management systems
* Clear communication skills and willingness to support and mentor others
* Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines
* Valid driver’s licence and willingness to travel to sites, including overnight stays where required

**Why join us**
  
We believe in more than just a job – we offer a place to grow, connect, and make a real impact.

* Grow With Us: Your development matters. We invest in your skills, support your career goals, and back you with opportunities to take on meaningful, challenging projects.
* Be Yourself: Our team is made stronger by the diverse voices and backgrounds that shape it. We foster a culture of inclusion, collaboration, and mutual respect.
* Make a Difference: Whether it’s helping clients, supporting communities, or tackling environmental challenges, your work here creates lasting, positive change – and we’ll encourage your ideas along the way.
* Live Well: We get that life isn’t all about work. That’s why we offer flexibility, team social events, rostered days off, benefits, and a team that supports you every step of the way.

If you are interested, please send an introductory letter with your updated CV to aditiagarwal@core-ep.com.au.

**About FACS**

At FACS, our mission is to make environments safer and healthier for the people who live and work in them. As one of the nation's leading environmental health consulting firms, we help organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. We are built on purpose, partnership, and performance, delivering measurable impact with every client engagement.

**Our Values**

We live our mission through three core values:

* **People First:** Support our team and clients, promote professional growth, and value collaboration.
* **Integrity of the Science:** Deliver accurate, reliable results through objective, evidence-based practices.
* **Client Relationships for Life:** Build long-term partnerships and help clients address environmental health challenges.

**Why Join Us**

* **Impact:** Contribute meaningful work that empowers teams and drives results across the organization.
* **Culture:** Thrive in a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and mission-driven environment where your work matters.
* **Growth:** Innovate, develop your skills, and help shape the future of how we operate and deliver on our mission.
* **Visibility:** Partner directly with leadership and cross-functional teams to make a real difference.

**About the Role:**

The Environmental Health Specialist will support public health and well-being by conducting fieldwork and environmental assessments for a variety of environmental health and industrial hygiene projects. Under the direction of Project Managers, you will support projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.

This is a field-based role that requires regular travel to local client sites and occasional travel outside the local area, depending on project needs. You will collect samples and field data, document site conditions, prepare accurate field notes, and communicate project updates to Project Managers.

This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys hands-on work, takes pride in accuracy and professionalism, and is eager to develop technical experience in environmental health and industrial hygiene. The ideal candidate demonstrates strong attention to detail, reliability, a positive work ethic, and a willingness to learn beyond their current comfort zone.

**Responsibilities:**

* Perform assigned fieldwork and project tasks under the direction of Project Managers.
* Travel regularly to local client sites and occasionally to out-of-area locations based on project needs.
* Support environmental health and industrial hygiene projects involving asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, air and exposure sampling, and other environmental health concerns.
* Review project scopes, site requirements, and field protocols to ensure a clear understanding of assigned work.
* Collect field data and samples in accordance with established procedures, project specifications, and safety requirements.
* Conduct site observations and document field conditions accurately and thoroughly.
* Prepare, organize, maintain, and transport the tools, equipment, and supplies needed for assigned fieldwork.
* Maintain detailed field notes; compile data; and summarize findings to support project reporting and analysis.
* Communicate regularly with Project Managers regarding project status, technical questions, field conditions, and next steps.
* Report progress, concerns, and deviations from project scope or established protocols promptly.
* Interact professionally and collaboratively with clients, contractors, building occupants, and other stakeholders at project sites.
* Follow all company safety procedures and use required personal protective equipment.
* Participate actively in training, mentorship, and professional-development opportunities to build technical knowledge in environmental health and industrial hygiene.
* Support the delivery of high-quality, timely client service while maintaining FACS’s standards for accuracy, professionalism, and integrity.

**What You Bring:**

**Required**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and attention to detail.
* Reliable, professional, and able to follow field protocols, safety requirements, and project instructions.
* Valid driver’s license, reliable transportation, current auto insurance, and a driving record that meets company standards.
* Ability to travel regularly to local client sites, with occasional out-of-area travel as needed.
* Ability to perform the essential functions of this field-based role, with or without reasonable accommodation.
* Flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends based on project requirements.

**Preferred**

* Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in a related field.
* Fieldwork or related experience in environmental services, construction, facilities, EHS, restoration, inspection, sampling, or technical documentation.
* Familiarity with asbestos, lead, mold and moisture, indoor environmental quality, or air and exposure sampling

**Physical & Work Requirements**

* Physical ability to stoop, kneel, climb, crawl, walk, and stand for extended periods in varied work environments while performing sampling activities
* Ability to lift and carry equipment weighing up to 50 lbs.
* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer for documentation and reporting
* Must be able to pass a background check, annual medical examinations, and OSHA-required respirator fit tests
* Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance
* Ability to travel locally to assigned client and project sites

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist (NEC)
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Environmental Scientist will undertake specialised environmental science duties involving the investigation, assessment and monitoring of environmental conditions, including soil, water, land and other natural resources.

The position will contribute to the identification of environmental risks, assessment of potential environmental impacts and development of appropriate management and mitigation strategies.

The successful candidate will work both independently and collaboratively with operational personnel, management, contractors and relevant stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

The successful applicant will be responsible for:

* Conducting environmental field investigations, inspections and scientific assessments to identify existing environmental conditions and potential environmental risks.
* Collecting, analysing and interpreting soil, water and other environmental samples to assess contamination, pollution levels and environmental quality.
* Monitoring environmental conditions and evaluating the impacts of operational and project activities on surrounding land, water, ecosystems and natural resources.
* Undertaking environmental assessments and investigations to identify potential impacts associated with construction, civil works, land disturbance and other operational activities.
* Developing, implementing and reviewing environmental management plans, procedures and control measures to minimise adverse environmental impacts.
* Identifying environmental hazards, non-compliance issues and potential risks, and recommending appropriate corrective and preventative actions.
* Providing scientific advice and technical recommendations to management regarding environmental protection, pollution prevention, land management and environmental compliance.
* Preparing detailed environmental assessment reports, technical documentation, monitoring reports and recommendations based on scientific findings and collected data.
* Assessing environmental data, identifying trends and interpreting scientific results to support operational and environmental management decisions.
* Monitoring the effectiveness of environmental control measures and recommending improvements where necessary.
* Assisting with the development and implementation of environmental rehabilitation, remediation and land restoration strategies where required.
* Ensuring environmental activities are conducted in accordance with applicable Western Australian and Commonwealth environmental legislation, regulations, standards and guidelines.
* Liaising with regulatory authorities, environmental consultants, laboratories, contractors and other relevant stakeholders regarding environmental matters.
* Maintaining accurate records of environmental inspections, sampling activities, monitoring results, investigations and corrective actions.
* Providing environmental guidance and technical support to operational personnel to promote environmental awareness and responsible workplace practices.
* Investigating environmental incidents, assessing their potential impacts and recommending appropriate remedial and preventative measures.
* Essential Qualifications

Applicants must possess:

* A Bachelor Degree or higher qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Studies, Soil Science or another highly relevant environmental science discipline.
* Demonstrated technical knowledge of environmental assessment, scientific investigation and environmental monitoring.
* Strong understanding of soil and water sampling, environmental testing and scientific data analysis.
* Knowledge of relevant environmental legislation, regulatory requirements and environmental management principles.

Essential Skills and Experience

The successful candidate will demonstrate:

* Relevant professional experience in environmental science, environmental investigations or a closely related scientific discipline.
* Experience undertaking environmental fieldwork, inspections and sampling activities.
* Ability to analyse and interpret scientific and environmental data.
* Experience preparing technical reports and environmental documentation.
* Knowledge of environmental risk identification, impact assessment and mitigation strategies.
* Understanding of environmental compliance requirements and environmental management systems.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving and technical report-writing skills.
* Ability to work independently and manage multiple responsibilities.
* Effective communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
* A practical approach to identifying environmental issues and developing scientifically supported solutions.

Pay: $79,423.00 – $90,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Visa sponsorship

Experience:

* Environmental services: 3 years (Required)

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Principal Geologist or Scientist - Environmental Assessment and Remediation
jobs.description:
Overview

Are you interested in building a meaningful career that can help make a positive impact on the world?

At Geosyntec, we partner with clients to solve complex challenges at the intersection of the environment, water, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. We are seeking a Principal Geologist or Scientist
to help lead and grow our Environmental Assessment and Remediation
practice in California, with an emphasis on supporting the Fresno office, Central Valley market, and broader Northern California operations.

This is a high-impact leadership opportunity for an accomplished environmental consultant with strong technical expertise, established client relationships, and a proven ability to develop, sell, manage, and deliver complex environmental investigation and remediation programs. The successful candidate will help strengthen Geosyntec’s regional presence, expand our environmental consulting capabilities, and support strategic growth across industrial, municipal, energy, solid waste, transportation, and government markets.

In this role, you will provide senior technical leadership, client and business development vision, project delivery oversight, and people leadership for multidisciplinary teams working on complex environmental assessment, remediation, compliance, and restoration projects. You will mentor and develop high-performing staff, cultivate long-term client relationships, and collaborate with regional and national leaders to deliver innovative, technically sound, and practical solutions.

Our work includes a broad range of technically challenging and high-value projects, such as:

Environmental site assessment, site characterization, and remedial investigations involving soil, groundwater, soil vapor, sediment, and surface water.
Remediation planning, feasibility studies, remedial design, remedy implementation, construction oversight, and long-term operations, maintenance, and monitoring.
Vapor intrusion assessment and mitigation, soil gas investigations, risk evaluation support, and regulatory strategy development.
Projects involving petroleum hydrocarbons, chlorinated solvents, metals, PFAS, PCBs, and other emerging or complex contaminants.
Regulatory programs and projects involving the California Regional Water Quality Control Boards, DTSC, CUPAs, CERCLA, RCRA, CalEPA programs, and local agencies.
Technical strategy, permitting support, stakeholder engagement, and advisory services for public- and private-sector clients.

Our clients span the industrial, institutional, energy, solid waste, transportation, municipal, and public-sector markets, offering the opportunity to work on impactful projects that address critical environmental and resource challenges.

This Position Offers The Opportunity To

Lead and grow a strategic environmental assessment and remediation practice in California, with a focus on Fresno, the Central Valley, and Northern California.
Develop and expand client relationships across environmental, industrial, energy, solid waste, transportation, public-sector, and private-sector markets.
Serve as a Client Manager, Account Lead, or senior technical advisor for key strategic clients.
Work on complex projects that address critical environmental, groundwater, remediation, compliance, and infrastructure challenges.
Collaborate with recognized technical experts across Geosyntec’s national and international consulting platform.
Make a lasting impact through strategic growth, mentorship, technical excellence, and exceptional client service.

Geosyntec is an innovative, international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public-sector clients to address new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.

We invest in our people. Each employee is unique, and your career at Geosyntec will be too. We offer competitive pay and benefits, and well-being programs to support you and your family.

To Learn More Visit: http://www.geosyntec.com/careers/ .

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Lead business development strategy for the Fresno office, Central Valley market, and broader California environmental assessment and remediation practice, including identifying opportunities, developing client relationships, expanding existing accounts, and leading proposal efforts.
Serve as a Client Manager, Account Lead, or senior technical advisor for one or more strategic clients.
Provide senior technical leadership for environmental investigation, remediation, compliance, restoration, and long-term monitoring projects.
Lead complex, multidisciplinary projects from planning through delivery, including scope development, technical strategy, investigation design, feasibility evaluation, remedial design, permitting, construction support, regulatory negotiation, quality review, risk management, and client engagement.
Direct preparation and review of technical reports, work plans, feasibility studies, remedial action plans, design documents, permit applications, regulatory submittals, proposals, and client correspondence.
Manage project performance, including scope, budgets, resources, schedules, quality standards, profitability, contracts, subcontractors, and multidisciplinary team coordination.
Set practice vision, support recruiting and team development, mentor staff, and help drive strategic growth for the Fresno office and Northern California operations.
Collaborate with professionals from multiple disciplines and offices to provide integrated, practical, and future-ready solutions for clients.
Represent Geosyntec in meetings, presentations, and negotiations with clients, regulators, teaming partners, contractors, industry groups, and other stakeholders.
Interpret and summarize technical data and regulatory requirements to support sound scientific conclusions and defensible client recommendations.
Promote and model a strong health and safety culture, which is fundamental to our operations.
Complete required OSHA/MSHA health and safety, first aid, CPR training, and medical monitoring, as applicable and paid for by the firm.
Drive personal, company, and rental vehicles to client, project, office, and other business locations, as needed.

Education and Licensure

Bachelor’s degree in geology, hydrogeology, earth sciences, environmental science, or a closely related science field. (required)
Advanced degree in geology, hydrogeology, environmental science, or a related discipline. (preferred)
California Professional Geologist (P.G.) license or other professional certification. (preferred)

Skills, Experience And Qualifications

At least 10 years of directly relevant environmental consulting experience, including significant client development and project management responsibilities; or equivalent combination of education and experience. (required)
Consulting experience with investigation and remediation of contaminated soil, groundwater, soil vapor, sediment, and vapor intrusion issues. (required)
Experience with contaminants including petroleum hydrocarbons, metals, chlorinated solvents, PFAS, PCBs, and/or emerging contaminants. (required)
Strong understanding of California environmental regulatory programs, including DTSC, Regional Water Quality Control Boards, CERCLA, RCRA, CUPA programs, and other CalEPA or local agency requirements. (required)
Demonstrated success developing client relationships, leading business development efforts, winning work, and growing consulting services. (required)
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and mentoring early-, mid-, and senior-level professionals. (required)
Strong project, program, and financial management experience, including scope, budgets, resources, schedules, profitability, risk, quality, and client satisfaction. (required)
Experience preparing and supervising technical reports, proposals, work scopes, pricing, budgets, and project performance metrics. (required)
Ability to work collaboratively and influence across offices, practices, and disciplines, including with senior leadership, clients, regulators, teaming partners, and staff without direct reporting relationships. (required)
Strong oral and written communication, technical writing, presentation, negotiation, and client engagement skills. (required)
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced consulting environment, manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and travel to client facilities or project sites, as needed. (required)
Experience with remedial design, remedy construction, construction oversight, and operation and maintenance of environmental remedies. (preferred)
Experience supporting major industrial, municipal, energy, solid waste, transportation, or government clients. (preferred)
Established professional network and client relationships within California environmental markets. (preferred)
Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training and refreshers. (preferred)
Health and safety training, medical monitoring, and client-driven drug and background testing may be required.
Valid U.S. driver’s license and satisfactory driving record for business travel. (required)

jobs.description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description:

Arcadis is seeking an entry-level
Geologist/Environmental Scientist to join our team in San Francisco, CA or Concord, CA. While this position requires both field and office work, the candidate should expect to spend 50% to 75% of their time in the field.

You will have the opportunity to join a dedicated team in San Francisco, CA or Concord, CA that prioritizes mentorship and your professional growth. The team is committed to supporting your success and providing guidance as you navigate your role.

We are currently considering candidates available for an immediate start and those seeking a Summer 2027 start date.

As part of our Resilience Environment team, you’ll help improve quality of life.

Role accountabilities:

As part of this role, you will be responsible for assisting Project Managers (PMs) and Task Managers (TMs) in planning and executing environmental site characterization, investigation, and remediation tasks.

Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. It is essential to conduct fieldwork with a focus on health and safety.

Your core duties will include:

Prepare subcontracts and oversee the work of subcontractors.
Writing and preparing technical reports, work plans, letters, and memoranda
Office work may include task coordination, data compilation and interpretation, cost estimates, health & safety plan preparation, report writing, regulatory file reviews, proposal writing, project strategy development, schedule and budget management, and establishment of subcontracts.
Conduct field work including soil, groundwater, and/or vapor sampling in the field. Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time.

To be successful in this role, you should possess strong written and oral communication skills, be self-motivated, and exhibit independent thinking. You should be able to work effectively and efficiently in a team setting as well as independently and remotely. Successful candidates will demonstrate their ability to be adaptable, creative problem solvers who can work collaboratively as a team member.

In summary, this position encompasses both office work (task management, data analysis, report preparation, scope preparation, and client communications) as well as field work. Fieldwork will also be a key aspect of this position, which will offer you an opportunity to be trained to oversee drilling for soil sampling and groundwater well installation, groundwater sampling, subcontractor oversight, operation and maintenance of remediation systems, vapor intrusion/soil gas surveys, among other tasks. Additionally, Arcadis supports many of our client’s needs when unforeseen incidents occur, such as train derailments, pipeline releases, etc. An aspect of this role is supporting our National emergency response teams to ensure rapid protection of human health and the environment. This work is completed under the direction of trained incident responders and may require unanticipated travel and work outside standard business hours.

Field work will require regional business travel for up to 1-2 days per week on average. A few times per year, travel will be required within the U.S. for up to two weeks at a time. Estimated travel is up to 75% during the first two years, with travel reduced with career growth. By the third year, travel for field work is typically 50%. Travel expenses are reimbursable. A valid driver's license is required for the role.

Qualifications & Experience:

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s of Science in Geology, Hydrogeology, or closely related field (i.e., environmental science, physical science)

Preferred Qualifications

Master of Science degree in Geology or closely related field
Current OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training 

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity employer. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

Arcadis offers benefits for full time and part time positions. These benefits include medical, dental, and vision, EAP, 401K, STD, LTD, AD&D, life insurance, paid parental leave, reward & recognition program and optional benefits including wellbeing benefits, adoption assistance and tuition reimbursement. We offer nine paid holidays and 15 days PTO that accrue per year. The salary range for this position is $63,480- $95,220. Actual salaries will vary and are based on several factors, such as experience, education, budget, internal equity, project and location.

jobs.description:
Intermediate Permitting Specialist

Play an integral role in Worley Consulting’s Environmental & Sustainability (E&S) team, helping energy sector clients navigate environmental permitting and regulatory requirements while supporting the responsible development and delivery of complex projects across the United States.

You will work alongside experienced environmental practitioners, engineers and project professionals on projects spanning upstream, midstream and downstream energy, as well as emerging markets such as hydrogen, carbon capture, renewable power and biofuels. This is an opportunity to strengthen your technical expertise, gain meaningful client and regulatory exposure, and build your consulting career within a collaborative global organization.

Purpose of the role

As an Intermediate Permitting Specialist, you will support the planning, preparation and delivery of environmental permitting and regulatory solutions for energy and infrastructure projects.

You will help identify permitting requirements, prepare applications and technical documentation, maintain permit schedules and compliance requirements, and support engagement with clients, regulatory agencies and other stakeholders. Working with senior consultants and technical specialists, you will develop practical regulatory strategies that align environmental requirements with project objectives, schedules and delivery priorities.

The role offers a strong development pathway for an environmental professional who wants to deepen their permitting expertise, expand their client-facing capabilities and contribute to Worley Consulting’s continued growth in established and emerging energy markets.

Location(s)

This is a full-time, hybrid position based near a Worley U.S. office.

Desired locations: Houston TX, Long Beach or Monrovia CA, Chicago IL, Charleston WV, or Reading PA.

You will be collaborating with colleagues, clients and project teams across multiple locations. Travel to client meetings, regulatory engagements and project or field locations will be required based on project needs.

You Will Be Responsible For

Support environmental permitting, regulatory and advisory services for energy and infrastructure projects.
Identify federal, state and local permitting requirements and help develop strategies aligned with project objectives and schedules.
Prepare compliant permit applications, supporting technical studies, regulatory documentation and approval packages.
Support environmental permitting and reviews under NEPA, CEQA and other applicable federal, state and local frameworks.
Develop and maintain permit matrices, tracking tools, schedules and compliance databases to track regulatory milestones, permit conditions and mitigation commitments.
Prepare and review accurate, high-quality technical correspondence, environmental reports, work plans, project documentation, cost estimates and schedules.
Collaborate with senior environmental professionals, engineers and project teams to integrate permitting into multidisciplinary project planning and execution.
Engage with regulators, clients and project stakeholders, developing communication and consulting skills to support successful project outcomes.
Support project management by coordinating assigned tasks and tracking scope, schedule, budget and progress.
Support proposals, scope development, cost estimates and opportunity identification.
Support quality assurance and alignment with Worley’s E&S systems, technical standards and HSE expectations.
Participate in client meetings and field programs, traveling as needed for effective project delivery.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

You will bring a foundation in environmental permitting or regulatory consulting combined with strong technical writing, analytical and collaboration skills. You will be motivated to expand your expertise and take on increasing responsibility as part of multidisciplinary project teams.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, Biology or a related discipline.
Typically 3–7 years of relevant experience, preferably in environmental consulting, engineering or regulation.
Working knowledge of U.S. environmental permitting, including NEPA and applicable federal and state requirements.
Familiarity with federal regulations, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act and Endangered Species Act.
Understanding of environmental compliance and permitting, including air and/or water requirements.
Experience supporting environmental permitting and preparing accurate, organized technical and regulatory documentation.
Demonstrated ability to track assigned project scope, schedules and budgets and identify potential variances.
Strong technical writing, reporting and documentation skills focused on quality, accuracy and detail.
Developing client-facing and stakeholder engagement skills; effective communication with clients, regulators and project teams.
Strong communication and collaboration skills for effective multidisciplinary teamwork.
Commitment to health, safety, environmental stewardship and responsible project delivery.
Motivation to build technical and consulting skills with guidance from experienced practitioners.

Additional Preferred Experience

Air quality permitting support experience and exposure to emissions modeling or regulatory strategy development.
Familiarity with CEQA and California environmental permitting requirements.
Exposure to environmental engineering, including stormwater management and Spill Prevention, Control and Countermeasure (SPCC) planning.
Experience supporting proposals, cost estimates or project planning.
Experience or demonstrated interest in emerging energy sectors, including hydrogen, carbon capture and management, renewable power and biofuels.

Compensation

For California applicants

Salary Range: $85,398 - $113,821; based upon experience
Benefits: eligible for PTO, 401k, medical, vision, dental, etc.

Los Angeles

We will consider for employment all qualified Applicants, including those with Criminal Histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles' Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

Application of the pay band: Variation in salary is determined by factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, relevant years of experience, geographic location, internal pay equity, and prevailing market conditions for the specific role.

Benefits

Feel the energy at Worley with access to a range of benefits including paid time off, holiday pay (usually 8 per year in the US), and eligibility to participate in the medical, life, dental, and vision insurance plans, as well as 401K plan.

Apply today

Bring your environmental permitting experience, curiosity and collaborative approach to a role where you can contribute to meaningful projects while continuing to develop as a trusted environmental professional.

You will have the opportunity to learn from experienced practitioners, work across multidisciplinary teams, gain exposure to clients and regulators, and broaden your experience across established and emerging energy markets. As your expertise develops, you will have opportunities to take on greater technical, project delivery and client responsibilities.

About Us

Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. We specialize in consulting, engineering, procurement and construction across the project lifecycle, with services extending through to operations and decommissioning. Leveraging extensive experience and AI-enabled delivery, we support customers in navigating complexity as they meet today’s needs and transition to more sustainable solutions. Join us and help drive innovation and sustainability in our projects.
