Job Description

Expression of Interest - Engineers | Technicians | Project Managers | Environmental Scientists

Bring your expertise. Build something meaningful— and a great life — in Bundaberg.

Are you an experienced technical or project professional looking for greater influence, meaningful regional work and the opportunity to grow your leadership career?

Join GHD’s close-knit Bundaberg team and help shape projects that support communities across the Wide Bay. You’ll enjoy the visibility and connection of a regional office, backed by the capability, opportunities and multidisciplinary expertise of GHD’s wider Queensland and global network.

GHD is seeking Expressions of Interest
from experienced professionals interested in joining our Bundaberg team and leading our growth and presence across the Wide Bay region.

We’re deliberately keeping our search broad. Your project management or technical background could be in transport, civil, water, structural, electrical, environment or another technical discipline. What matters most is your ability to bring strong consulting experience, work closely with clients and contribute to both project delivery and business growth.

Build your career, and a great life, in Bundaberg

A move to Bundaberg could mean creating more space for what matters while continuing to work on meaningful projects, build trusted client relationships and grow your professional influence.

Bundaberg combines the serenity of coastal living with a strong sense of community and connection. The region is the closest mainland gateway to Lady Musgrave and Lady Elliot islands — two of the Southern Great Barrier Reef’s finest coral cays — and is surrounded by beaches, mangroves, and other ecosystems that support diverse marine life.

The region also offers the everyday essentials that make relocation easier: accessibility to Brisbane, modern schools, growing recreational opportunities, and high-quality healthcare facilities and upgrades. A diversified regional economy supports employment, investment and a lifestyle that guarantees a rewarding alternative to the hustle and bustle of major-city living.

At GHD, you’ll become part of a close-knit local team where your contribution will be visible and valued. You’ll work alongside people with deep regional knowledge while being widely supported by multidisciplinary colleagues across Queensland and GHD’s global network. It’s an opportunity to build local relationships, broaden your experience and make a lasting impact on the communities around you.

Discover what life in the Bundaberg region could offer you.

What could your opportunity look like?

Depending on your experience and background, you could join us as an Engineer, Technician, Project Manager or Environmental Scientist. In our Bundaberg team, you’ll have the opportunity to work across disciplines, build strong relationships with regional clients and play a visible role in the continued growth of our Wide Bay business.

Regional consulting can offer broader exposure and greater influence. You may find yourself working more closely with clients, contributing across the full project lifecycle and helping shape opportunities from their earliest stages — while still having access to the technical depth and career pathways of a global professional services company.

You may already be an established senior professional, or you may be ready to broaden your influence, take on greater client and commercial responsibility and continue developing towards future leadership opportunities.

This opportunity isn’t defined by a single technical discipline. We’re looking for the right capability, consulting mindset and client orientation to complement our Bundaberg team and contribute to our continued growth across the region.

What You’ll Bring

We’d like to hear from you if you bring:

5 plus years’ experience in consulting, technical delivery or project management
A background in engineering, environment, project management or another relevant technical discipline
Strong client-facing and relationship-building capability
A commercial mindset and an interest in identifying and developing opportunities
The ability and willingness to contribute directly to project delivery
A collaborative approach and the ability to work across disciplines, projects and locations
An interest in contributing to the continued growth of our Bundaberg business
The ambition to continue developing your career and potentially move into broader leadership over time
Relevant professional accreditation for your discipline, such as RPEQ and/or CPEng, or working towards attaining accreditation where applicable

You don’t need to already know the Queensland market. We’re interested in professionals who bring the right consulting and client-focused approach, valuable experience and a willingness to collaborate with colleagues who have strong local market knowledge.

Why GHD?

At GHD, you’ll have the opportunity to combine your technical expertise, project experience and client relationships while being connected to a broader multidisciplinary business.

This isn’t about fitting into a narrowly defined role. We’re interested in what you could bring to Bundaberg.

Whether you’re an experienced engineer, project manager, technical specialist or consultant looking for greater influence, broader client exposure and an opportunity to contribute to regional growth, we’d like to hear from you.

Could Bundaberg be your next move?

Register your interest and start a confidential conversation with us about your experience, career goals and what life and work with GHD in Bundaberg could look like. Explore the region at bundabergregion.org.

GHD is an equal opportunity employer, and we want everyone to be able to fully participate in our recruitment process. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and people of all identities.

GHD embraces a range of flexible work practices to create a work environment focused on well-being, flexibility and productivity where our people can thrive.

We respectfully ask that no agency resumes be presented at this stage.

About Us

Come together and make a meaningful impact.

We bring our people together to create something bigger and solve some of the world's most complex problems. Come and experience the power of commitment and see strategy and ideas come to life when you join GHD.

Let's drive real change.

Our Pledge to You

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.

That’s the #PowerOfCommitment

Who We Are

GHD is a global professional services company that leads through engineering, architecture, and construction expertise. We are an employee-owned company with over 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals, across more than 200 offices spanning five continents.

The Power of Commitment is our brand promise. It’s what makes us different. We are bound to our stated vision and determination to address humanity’s most urgent needs: to make water, energy and urbanisation sustainable for generations to come.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  
  
Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory), the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) serves as the supervisor for professional scientific staff within the Department of Pesticide Regulation’s (DPR) Pesticide Use Reporting (PUR) Program. This position plans, directs, and evaluates scientific, technical, and programmatic activities supporting the accuracy, completeness, accessibility, and effective use of statewide pesticide use data. The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) oversees PUR data quality and reporting activities, including quality assurance and quality control processes, development of the annual PUR report, responses to data requests, and technical support for urgent or complex data needs. The position provides technical and programmatic leadership on pesticide use reporting requirements, database and data system improvements, and changes resulting from legislation, regulation, and Department policy. The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) supports implementation of Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Branch and Department priorities and follows direction and guidance provided by the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory), Branch Chief, and executive leadership.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

* Work primarily in an office building in a climate-controlled environment and under artificial lighting
* May be required to sit for long periods at a time
* Must be able to use a computer monitor, mouse, and keyboard for up to 8 hours per day
* Must be able to lift at least 10 pounds
* Occasional travel, sometimes requiring overnight stays, to conduct site visits or attend training events or workshops may be required.
* Site visits may require walking in agricultural fields and orchards and in natural areas with moderate slopes, unpaved grounds, and uneven surfaces, such as ploughed fields and grassy meadows, undeveloped roads, ditches, levees, and other structures located adjacent to agricultural fields. Site visits may also occur in urban and suburban environments. Site visits will occur under various climatic conditions that may require exposure to high heat, full sun, high humidity, wind, and rain.

Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.
  
  
**Beginning July 1st, 2026, it is anticipated this position will be office-centered and employees will be expected to report to the office at least four days per week.**

jobs.description:
Grounded in safety, quality, and ethics, our experts lead their fields and guide our work with rigor, a creative spirit, and a vision for growth. We draw from more than 20 technical specialties worldwide and are committed to fostering an inclusive community of diverse talents, backgrounds, and expertise. We’re a place to apply your passion and collaborate with top environmental talents on work critical to our clients and the communities they support. Join a team that has the environment down to a science.

Your Opportunity

Stantec is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist to serve as a Planning Waters Team Lead for a large utility client within our environmental planning and natural resources practice. This position will provide technical and operational leadership for planning-related waters work, including jurisdictional waters and aquatic resources assessments, regulatory permitting, technical documentation, and environmental review.

The successful candidate will function as an experienced professional who applies advanced practical knowledge, exercises independent judgment, and resolves complex technical and project-delivery issues within established professional and regulatory practices. The role will also provide mentoring, work coordination, quality oversight, and technical direction to environmental scientists and other multidisciplinary team members.

Location

This role is based out of our Stantec office in San Diego, CA; however geographic alignment with other Stantec offices can be considered based on experience. Stantec offers flexible work locations (including working from home), flexible work hours, and a robust compensation and benefits package. Typical office environment working with computers and remaining sedentary for long periods of time.

Your Key Responsibilities

Provide technical and functional leadership for planning-related waters assignments, including aquatic resource evaluations, jurisdictional waters delineations, desktop assessments, field investigations, permitting, and environmental documentation.
Coordinate team workloads, assign or recommend assignments based on staff qualifications and availability, monitor schedules and deliverables, and identify resource needs or delivery risks.
Provide technical direction, coaching, mentoring, and quality-control support to junior and intermediate staff.
Develop regulatory strategies for projects requiring aquatic resource approvals or consultation.
Prepare and review permit applications and supporting materials associated with Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, Waste Discharge Requirements, and California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements, as applicable.
Prepare, review, and provide quality assurance and quality control for jurisdictional waters delineation reports, Aquatic Resources Delineation Reports, technical memoranda, biological resources reports, and permit packages.
Interpret federal, state, and local environmental requirements and advise project teams on applicable regulatory pathways, risks, data needs, and recommended next steps.
Coordinate with clients, project managers, technical specialists, and regulatory agencies regarding project requirements, technical findings, schedules, deliverables, and permitting strategies.
Lead or support agency coordination and negotiations, including responding to agency comments and requests for supplemental information.
Review work prepared by team members for technical accuracy, consistency, regulatory defensibility, completeness, and adherence to applicable quality standards.
Develop and improve team procedures, templates, quality-control tools, technical guidance, and training materials to support consistent project delivery.
Lead by example in applying Stantec and client health, safety, security, and environmental requirements.

Your Capabilities and Credentials

Advanced practical knowledge of aquatic resources, jurisdictional waters, wetlands, streams, riparian systems, and related environmental planning and permitting requirements.
Working knowledge of the Clean Water Act, including Sections 404 and 401; applicable state water-quality requirements; Waste Discharge Requirements; and California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 requirements.
Experience developing aquatic resource permitting strategies and preparing or reviewing permit applications and supporting technical documentation.
Ability to independently evaluate complex technical and regulatory issues, interpret available information, and recommend practical, defensible solutions.
Demonstrated ability to lead technical workstreams, coordinate workloads, guide teams, and deliver assignments within established scope, budget, schedule, and quality expectations.
Experience mentoring staff, reviewing technical work, providing constructive feedback, and supporting employee development.
Strong technical writing, editing, verbal communication, presentation, and organizational skills.
Ability to communicate technical information clearly to clients, project managers, multidisciplinary teams, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
Ability to build productive professional relationships and work collaboratively across offices, disciplines, and business lines.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to technically accurate, complete, and high-quality deliverables.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and Adobe Acrobat.
Must have valid driver's license and clean MVR

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, biology, ecology, wetland science, natural resources, soil science, botany, environmental planning, or a related discipline.

Minimum of five years of directly related professional experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Experience successfully leading the technical aspects of small to medium projects or significant workstreams within larger, multidisciplinary projects.

Experience supporting utility, energy, transportation, infrastructure, restoration, or land-development projects is preferred.

This description is not a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that may be required of the employee and other duties, responsibilities and activities may be assigned or may be changed at any time with or without notice.

About Stantec

Stantec is a global leader in sustainable engineering, architecture, and environmental consulting. The diverse perspectives of our partners and interested parties drive us to think beyond what’s previously been done on critical issues like climate change, digital transformation, and future-proofing our cities and infrastructure. We innovate at the intersection of community, creativity, and client relationships to advance communities everywhere, so that together we can redefine what’s possible.
